findingDetails.title: The strategy updater duplicates a machine-owned heading it was meant to normalize
findingDetails.claim: replaceAnchorSection writes the heading inside its replacement and takes that branch whenever the anchor markers exist, so a heading-first strategy keeps the author's heading and gains a second one; a second pass leaves both.
findingDetails.scopeProof: The reducer is the only writer of that block, the duplicate is visible in this lineage's strategy, and a second identical pass did not remove it.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Read both branches of replaceAnchorSection and the heading fallback; re-ran the reducer on the same input and counted the heading, which stayed at two.
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: The duplicate may be read as a second authored section rather than a defect.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: Withdraw if the strategy template is changed to place the heading inside the anchor markers, or if the updater drops a heading immediately above the anchor.

findingDetails.title: A direction ruled out once is rendered as a blocked approach that must not be retried
findingDetails.claim: buildExhaustedApproaches folds iteration.ruledOut into the exhausted section and renders each entry as BLOCKED (1 attempts) with 'Repeated iteration evidence ruled this direction out' and 'Do NOT retry', so one pass of evidence freezes the direction.
findingDetails.scopeProof: The renderer is the only producer of that section; its three fixed lines are visible in this lineage's strategy for four one-pass directions.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Read the renderer and the template's section contract; checked the rendered output, which shows four such entries with '1 attempts'.
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: Folding ruled-out directions into one do-not-repeat list may be deliberate economy, and 'Do NOT retry' may mean 'do not re-open without new evidence'.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: Withdraw if the template or the state-format doc states that ruled-out directions are intentionally frozen after one pass.
